name: The stock shed at Newberry & Dole's South Branch plant

documented_range.note: NO SOURCE RECORD DATES THIS BUILDING, BECAUSE NO SOURCE RECORD NAMES IT. The bracket is the plant's own, carried across without being re-argued: `newberry_dole_slaughterhouse_south_branch`, the plant Andreas records Oliver Newberry and George W. Dole having erected on the South Branch in 1834 (scan p. 1151) carries 1834-01-01 to 1835-12-31, the year documented and the month not, and a works building that serves that plant cannot honestly claim to have stood before the plant or after the last date the plant's record needs. It is graded `reconstructed`, as the building is.

position.symbolic_location: On the east bank of the South Branch below the town, the southernmost building of Newberry & Dole's works, across a cart yard from the salt house, facing the branch with its stable door on that yard - the end of the band the stock reaches first coming up the branch from the prairie.
position.note:
INVENTED, AND SEATED BY THE WORKS RULE BELOW. WHY THE BAND RUNS SOUTH ALONG THE BANK AND NOT BEHIND THE PLANT: behind is east, and east is Market Street - `tools/plat_corridors.corridors()` puts its platted corridor at local E 73.00 to E 97.00 across this reach and the plant already stands 1.30 m inside its west edge. North is Randolph's corridor, local N -265.00 to N -241.00, which the plant stands 11.45 m inside. So the three works buildings stand SOUTH of the plant in the order the work runs, every one of them with its east wall on local E 72.500 - 0.50 m clear of Market's corridor edge - so the band reads as one row and not as three seatings. THIS BUILDING'S NORTHING: its north wall stands 5.20 m south of the salt house's south wall, at local N -289.934. WHY IT IS AT THE SOUTH END: the band is set out in the order the work runs, and beasts driven in off the prairie meet the works before the works meets the river - so the stock stands at the landward end and the barrels leave from the end nearest the town. That is an argument from the trade and not a source. MEASURED ON THIS SEAT, over a 25 x 25 lattice on the placed polygon: the ground stands 0.465 m to 0.695 m above the committed water surface - dry everywhere - with 0.230 m of relief, inside the 0.30 m clause; `intrusion` reads it clear of all 33 platted corridors; and no committed footprint stands within 14 m of it. WORKING UNCERTAINTY IS TOTAL.

THE WORKS RULE, STATED ONCE AND APPLIED SIX TIMES (T-1709). Every one of the four documented noxious trades on the branches records, in its own footprint note, that the works are outside its polygon: `newberry_dole_slaughterhouse_south_branch` says 'the pens, the yard and the barrelling and salting space that a packing operation needs are outside the footprint and outside this archetype, which builds a building rather than a works'; `miller_tannery` says 'a tannery is its yard - bark mill, lime pits, tan vats, drying sheds, and a water supply - and none of that is in this polygon or in the model'; `clybourn_slaughterhouse` says 'what is not modelled is arguably the bigger half'; `elston_soap_candle_manufactory` gives a shed 'big enough for a rendering kettle, a cooling and moulding floor and an ash leach' and nothing beside it. This building is one of the works those four sentences name, and NOTHING ATTESTS IT. It is placed by a rule and not by a plate. THE RULE: (1) a works building stands BEHIND its plant, on the side away from the water, because the plant's own bearing puts its working face on the water and the ground behind it is what is left; (2) the gap between the plant's wall and the works' wall is 5.20 m, the cart yard T-1640 derived from `data/yard/town_trade_goods.json` - 1.00 m of clearance from the wall a wagon stands at, plus the 3.20 m of ground a parked wagon needs, plus 1.00 m from the wall opposite - and the same 5.20 m separates one works building from the next, so the whole band is set out on one committed figure; (3) the works take the plant's own bearing, so the yard between them is square and the doors face it; (4) where the ground behind the plant is a platted street corridor, the works stand ALONG the bank instead, in the order the work runs, on a line that keeps them 0.50 m clear of that corridor's own edge - which is what the South Branch band does, because Market Street's corridor runs E 73.00 to E 97.00 at this reach and the plant itself stands 1.30 m inside it. THE FOUR PREDICATES each seat is held to, on a 25 x 25 lattice over the placed polygon: dry in the committed heightfield (`data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut`, WATER_SURFACE_M = 0), relief inside the 0.30 m `generate_block_infill.MAX_RELIEF_M` allows, clear of all 33 platted corridors (`tools/plat_corridors.intrusion`), and clear of every footprint the committed tree already places. docs/RESEARCH/branch_noxious_works.md carries the readings and docs/LIBERTIES.md L284 owns the invention.

derivation.reason: The two machine-checkable methods this project has are a platted corner and a traced waterline, and this seat is neither: it is a stated setback from a committed neighbouring building, on that building's own bearing, held clear of a committed corridor edge and tested against the committed heightfield. Every input is committed and the rule is written out in position.note, so it reproduces by hand; no derivation method in the schema can recompute it, and declaring one that could not would be worse than declaring none.

footprint.note: INVENTED. 5.4864 x 7.9248 m is 18 x 26 ft, the floor of family A1's band (18-26 ft front, 20-32 ft deep) - the crosswalk's lofted stable, the family whose visible signature is a stable door and ventilation. The floor of the band rather than the middle of it, because this is a holding shed for stock waiting to be killed and for the plant's own draught oxen, not a livery. The documented throughput constrains the order of magnitude and nothing finer: 300 cattle across a whole season is a few beasts standing at a time, not a herd. Every number is invented.

construction.note: Sawn boards nailed up vertically, the archetype's `plank`, the same fabric as the packing house at the other end of the band. Invented.

wall_height_m.note: About 9 ft 10 in, a little over the archetype's size-aware default of 2.88 m for this plan, because a beast is led in under a tie beam and an ox stands 5 ft at the shoulder with its head up. What is reasoned is the range. Invented.

roof_type.note: 7.92 m of depth is past the 5.0 m at which `default_roof_type` stops giving a shed roof. Invented.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The archetype's own default for a gable, stated. Invented.

door.note: A beast led through in hand, 1.35 m clear - the archetype's own term and the one thing this family exists to get right. It stands on a 7.92 m wall. Invented.

door_side.note: The `right` elevation is the max-x wall, which at this bearing faces NORTH, onto the cart yard between this shed and the salt house. Invented.

phases.change_note: One phase. This is a reconstruction of a works building the plant's own record says is missing, not a record of a building anybody named, so it has no history to divide into phases and inventing one would be inventing twice.

function.note: The closed vocabulary has no `stock shed`; `stable` is family A1's own term and the nearest it carries. The specific use - holding beasts before the kill, and the plant's own draught oxen - is in the record's NAME and in this note. The use comes from the plant. A slaughter-house that took 300 head of cattle and 1,400 hogs in a season held stock somewhere before it killed them, and the plant's own record says the pens and the stock yard are outside its footprint and outside its archetype. This record models the roofed half of that; the pens themselves are a fence line and this archetype builds buildings. No occupant is claimed and no animal is drawn.

research_note: A RECONSTRUCTED WORKS BUILDING, THE THIRD AND LAST OF THE SOUTH BRANCH BAND - T-1709, of T-1203. WHAT IS HELD: Andreas's packing chapter (scan p. 1151) for the plant and its throughput. WHAT IS INVENTED: this building and every attribute of it. WHAT IS STILL NOT MODELLED, and the plant's own record already says so: the killing pens and the stock yard, which are enclosures rather than buildings - the same half `outbuilding_params` declines in as many words and the same half docs/LIBERTIES.md L10 has been carrying for the Western Hotel's wagon yard. Adding a roof does not discharge it. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE IT: any description of the South Branch plant beyond the sentence recording its erection. Built under the owner's standing ruling of 2026-08-18. Links: T-1709 - T-1203 - T-1640 - docs/RESEARCH/branch_noxious_works.md - docs/LIBERTIES.md L284.
